newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end limit up on interest rate ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end limit up on interest rate ideas.

text.p: A sharp rally in the bond market and resulting reduced concerns over interest rates continued to support CME lumber futures and May ended up the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf, traders said.
Lumber closed $10.00 to $1.00 per tbf higher with May up limit at $404.60 and July up $8.30 at $401.60 after being up the limit earlier.

"There had been some concern that the Fed was going to raise (interest) rates again -- apparently nobody thinks that's going to happen now," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

Futures traded uneven early in light of the lower cash lumber market with a fund rolling longs into July and a local selling July. But selling pressure lacked followthrough as financial markets continued to climb and lumber futures followed into buy stops, traders said.

Cash markets apparently remained unfazed by the sharp rally in futures and financial markets. Mills continue to look for buyers and are willing to take counter offers to move some of their production, cash sources said.
